newsitem.title: INDIA: At least 135 feared dead in Indian flash floods.
newsitem.headline: At least 135 feared dead in Indian flash floods.

text.p: At least 135 people were missing and feared dead on Tuesday after flash floods swept through a remote Himalayan region of northern India, police said.
Monsoon rains triggered the flooding in the Chirgaon region of the northern state of Himachal Pradesh, they said.
"It is feared that 135 people have been washed away. But so far only 50 bodies have been recovered," N.C. Joshi, a senior state police official, told Reuters.
Chirgaon is about 125 km (80 miles) east of the state capital Shimla in the Himalayan mountains.

"The floods have completely washed away the shopping area in Chirgaon," said Rakesh Aggarwal, deputy police chief. "Three bridges connecting the region were also swept away. The whole communication network has been paralysed."

Press Trust of India said the 135 missing were swept away after the Andhra River burst its banks and raged through a village. The river water damaged many buildings, washed away roads and drowned farm animals, it said.
Joshi said the army had been asked to help with rescue and relief operations.
